result.summary: Do not dispatch: act-time resolution failures can still leave live jobs behind while uninstall deletes their core.

findings.title: Stop deletion when the pre-unload re-check cannot resolve a schedule
findings.body: D6 drops a discovered path when its act-time lstat or resolution fails, then continues reversal. Consider an unrecorded plist discovered and disclosed successfully whose D5a re-check encounters EIO: no unload is attempted, but the manifest loop and disposeCoreMechanics still remove the core. If the error clears before D5b, its independent re-check also permits deleting the plist without any unload attempt. Thus 'failing can only ever preserve' is false for the complete uninstall. This recreates R-stripped-manifest-orphan; it is distinct from the deferred R-failed-unload because no spawn occurs.
findings.recommendation: Require non-absence resolution/lstat failures in D5a to stop uninstall before the manifest deletion loop and core sweep. Restrict D5b to candidates that passed D5a. Add a regression where discovery and disclosure succeed, the live D5a check throws EIO, and subsequent filesystem calls succeed; assert that the core, manifest and schedule file survive.

next_steps: Update D6, D15 and their acceptance tests to preserve recovery state when the pre-unload check fails.
